syntax: group_concat(value, separator) OVER (PARTITION BY team ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING)
summary: group_concat joins non-NULL values with a separator.
documentation: group_concat joins non-NULL values with a separator. An explicitly ordered full-partition window gives every row in a team the same deterministic concatenation, after which DISTINCT can return one summary per team.
inputs: members(id INTEGER, team TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT), with distinct ids and names containing no pipe character.
returns: team and names, one row per team, ordered by team.
caution: Concatenation order is not guaranteed without ordering the aggregate input or window. NULL names are skipped; a team with only NULL names gets NULL. This is not a lossless format when names can contain the separator.
scenarios: Create an ordered team roster label for a report.
Preview a sequence of approved category names in one cell.
Build a compact list of imported labels while skipping missing values.
title: Join ordered team names
problem: Return one row per team with names joined by | in ascending id order, skipping NULL names. Name the columns team and names, and order teams alphabetically. Use a full-partition ordered window and DISTINCT to retain teams with all NULL names.
hint: Apply group_concat as an ordered window before selecting distinct team summaries.
goal: Use group_concat() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
